# PR Review Cycle -- Inputs (full table)

Companion to `SKILL.md`; the variable names and rules here are normative.

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MODE` | `'local'` \| `'remote'` \| `'gate'` | `local`: run the pre-publication steps (1-6) only. `remote`: the PR already exists; run the post-publication steps (7-9) using the local-phase facts recorded by the prior `local` invocation. `gate`: answer "may this PR merge?" for a caller about to merge (Step 10) -- it runs no reviewer dispatch and fixes nothing. Steps 1 and 1b (scope and guidance) run in every mode: every phase reviews the same range under the same base-commit guidance. |
| `BASE_SHA` / `HEAD_SHA` | string | Already-resolved commit SHAs for the diff under review (never a bare ref). |
| `REVIEWED_TREE_SHA` | string (optional) | `MODE=local`: the tree of the head this review validates -- the post-fix head's tree id -- re-resolved after the batch fix exactly as the head is (Step 6). Passed as `reviewedTreeSha` and recorded in the state report, so a later `MODE=remote` run can tell the PR-creation commit holds the reviewed content. Leave it out when not computed. |
| `HEAD_TREE_SHA` | string (optional) | `MODE=remote`: the tree of `HEAD_SHA` -- its tree id. Passed as `headTreeSha` to `status` and as `treeSha` to `state-read`. Leave it out when not computed. |
| `MERGE_BASE_SHA`, `PR_BASE_SHA`, `PARENT_PHASE_TIP_SHA` | string (optional) | Passed through to CLI `scope`; Step 1 says which of them (and `BASE_SHA`) becomes the base. |
| `PR_ID` | string | Stable per-PR key (e.g. `<repo-slug>-pr-<number>` or `<repo-slug>-<branch>`) used to address the review-state report. |
| `PR_URL` | string (optional) | Known only once the PR is published; required for `MODE=remote`. |
| `TEST_COMMAND` | string | The fastest relevant test command discovered from the repository. |
| `SKIP_TESTS` | boolean | `--skip-tests` passthrough. When true the broad test gate is not run: record `tests.skipped = true` plus the command that would have run; status is then never `REVIEW_COMPLETE`, but `REVIEW_PENDING` with reason `tests skipped`. |
| `REVIEW_ONLY` | boolean | `MODE=local` for **someone else's PR**: the cycle reviews and reports, and fixes nothing. Step 5, and Step 6's verification and re-review, do not run (no batch fix, no post-fix verification, no re-review); Step 6's tests fact and security gate still do. The tests fact comes from CI when `CHECK_RUNS` shows a pass for `HEAD_SHA`, else from one local run, and `SKIP_TESTS` skips both (`reference/triage-fix-reverify.md`, "Review-only runs"). Passed as `reviewOnly` to `status`: the status is then `REVIEW_PENDING` with a reason and never `REVIEW_COMPLETE`, and `localPhase` is never `LOCAL_REVIEW_COMPLETE`. The `pr-review-request` router sets it for every PR target and never for local changes; only an explicit `true` makes a run review-only, so every other caller gets the full loop. |
| `CHECK_RUNS` | array (optional, `REVIEW_ONLY` only) | The host's check runs for exactly `HEAD_SHA`, each `{ id, name, commitSha, conclusion }` as the host returned it: `commitSha` is that run's own commit, and a run still going has no conclusion. Read by the caller, read-only; never filtered, summarised or completed by hand. Passed as `tests.checkRuns`: whether CI shows the tests passing is derived from them by the CLI and by nothing else. Leave the input out when the runs could not be read. |
| `CHECK_RUNS_TOTAL` | integer (with `CHECK_RUNS`) | The total the host reported for that listing (its `total_count`). Passed as `tests.totalCount`: the list counts as complete only when it holds exactly that many runs, so a first page of many never reads as the whole. |
| `FOREMAN` | boolean | When true, the interactive wait (Step 7) is never entered; see Foreman-mode rules below. |
| `BOT_LOGINS` | string[] | Configured review-bot usernames passed through to CLI `remote`. |
| `PR_BODY` | string (optional) | The PR description this cycle grades: in `MODE=local` the body the caller is about to publish, in `MODE=remote` the published one. Passed as `body` to CLI `description` (Step 1b). Callers get this check through the skill and never run the CLI themselves. |
| `AGENT_AUTHORED` | boolean | True when an agent drafted `PR_BODY`. Passed as `agentAuthored` to CLI `description`: an agent-authored body must also name the person accountable for it on a `Directed by:` line. Anything other than an explicit `false` is read as true -- an unset `AGENT_AUTHORED` included (leave the key out of the payload and the CLI reads it as true) -- so a claim nobody made, or one that cannot be read, never relaxes the check. A caller that cannot know who drafted the body leaves it unset and reports the grade as returned; it never passes `false` to make a body ready. |
| `PLAN_ONLY` | boolean | `MODE=local`: the caller wants to see the cost before spending it. Run Steps 1 to 1c, print the plan (tier, depth `mode` and `reasons`, reviewers and verifiers -- the `reviewerAssignments` of `slices`, one reviewer per slice and lens -- slices, time bound) and return it: no reviewer is dispatched and nothing is fixed, tested or written. No status is derived -- nothing has been reviewed, so there is none to report, and a plan is never a review result. |
| `REUSE_RECORDED` | boolean | `MODE=local`: the caller is asking again for a head it already had reviewed. Step 1a then returns the recorded result for this head and base instead of redoing the review. Leave it unset to review as before -- every caller except the `pr-review-request` router does -- and unset it when the person asked for the review to be redone. |
| `REVIEWER_COUNT` | integer (optional) | `MODE=local`: how many reviewers Step 1c plans, 2 to 4. Unset, it plans the mode's minimum (two at Standard and Deep, one at Quick), as it always has. Anything but an integer from 2 to 4 is refused: `REVIEW_BLOCKED` naming this input, nothing dispatched, never rounded or clamped. A valid count is spent as `lensesPerSlice` -- more DISTINCT lenses on every slice, never duplicate passes over the same range -- and graded like any plan: `depth` `violations` stay binding, so Quick keeps its one reviewer and a policy minimum above the count raises it, and the plan says which count was used -- and the verifier count and every bound are unchanged. The `pr-review-request` router sets it only when the person asked for more reviewers. |
| `PR_NUMBER` | string \| number | `MODE=gate`: the PR whose approvals and reviews are read from the host. |
| `DIRECTED_BY` | string (optional) | `MODE=gate`: the login of the person who directed an agent-authored PR, read from the body's `Directed by:` line. Passed as `directedBy` to CLI `approvals`, where it counts as one of the required reviewers (AC-014-3) only when `AGENT_AUTHORED` is true. It is a line the PR's author writes, so it never lowers a floor by itself: the solo-maintainer discount also needs that person's own `APPROVED` review of the head, unless they are the PR author, in which case it rests on their own credit as author-as-director (`solo-maintainer-self-credit`; `reference/merge-gate.md`, 10e). |
| `PROPOSED_TIER` | string (optional) | `MODE=gate`: a tier an agent or the author proposed. Passed to CLI `tier` as `proposedTier`; it can only ever raise (AC-013-2). |
| `CODE_OWNER_DECISION` | object (optional) | `MODE=gate`: `{ login, isCodeOwner }` for a proposal, checked against CODEOWNERS by the caller. Passed as `proposedBy`; only a code owner's decision can lower a tier. |
